lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: name: teach

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: disable-model-invocation: true

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: argument-hint: "What would you like to learn about?"

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The user has asked you to teach them something. This is a stateful request - they intend to learn the topic over multiple sessions.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Teaching Workspace

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Treat the current directory as a teaching workspace. The state of their learning is captured in this directory in several files:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `MISSION.md`: A document capturing the _reason_ the user is interested in the topic. This should be used to ground all teaching. Use the format in [MISSION-FORMAT.md](./MISSION-FORMAT.md).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `./reference/*.html`: A directory of reference materials. These are the compressed learnings from the lessons - cheat sheets, reference algorithms, syntax, yoga poses, glossaries. They are the raw units of learning. They should be beautiful documents which print out well, and are designed for quick reference.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `RESOURCES.md`: A list of resources which can be explored to ground your teaching in contextual knowledge, or to acquire knowledge and wisdom. Use the format in [RESOURCES-FORMAT.md](./RESOURCES-FORMAT.md).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `./learning-records/*.md`: A directory of learning records, which capture what the user has learned. These are loosely equivalent to architectural decision records in software development - they capture non-obvious lessons and key insights that may need to be revised later, or drive future sessions. These should be used to calculate the zone of proximal development. They are titled `0001-<dash-case-name>.md`, where the number increments each time. Use the format in [LEARNING-RECORD-FORMAT.md](./LEARNING-RECORD-FORMAT.md).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `./lessons/*.html`: A directory of lessons. A **lesson** is a single, self-contained HTML output that teaches one tightly-scoped thing tied to the mission. This is the primary unit of teaching in this workspace.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `./assets/*`: Reusable **components** shared across lessons. See [Assets](#assets).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - `NOTES.md`: A scratchpad for you to jot down user preferences, or working notes.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Philosophy

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: To learn at a deep level, the user needs three things:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Knowledge**, captured from high-quality, high-trust resources

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Skills**, acquired through highly-relevant interactive lessons devised by you, based on the knowledge

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Wisdom**, which comes from interacting with other learners and practitioners

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Before the `RESOURCES.md` is well-populated, your focus should be to find high-quality resources which will help the user acquire knowledge. Never trust your parametric knowledge.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Some topics may require more skills than knowledge. Learning more about theoretical physics might be more knowledge-based. For yoga, more skills-based.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Fluency vs Storage Strength

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: You should be careful to split between two types of learning:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Fluency strength**: in-the-moment retrieval of knowledge

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Storage strength**: long-term retention of knowledge

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Fluency can give the user an illusory sense of mastery, but storage strength is the real goal. Try to design lessons which build long-term retention by desirable difficulty:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Using retrieval practice (recall from memory)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Spacing (distributing practice over time)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Interleaving (mixing up different but related topics in practice - for skills practice only)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Lessons

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A lesson is the main thing you produce — the unit in which knowledge and skills reach the user. Each lesson is one self-contained HTML file, saved to `./lessons/` and titled `0001-<dash-case-name>.html` where the number increments each time.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A lesson should be **beautiful** — clean, readable typography and layout — since the user will return to these later to review. Think Tufte.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The lesson should be short, and completable very quickly. Learners' working memory is very small, and we need to stay within it. But each lesson should give the user a single tangible win that they can build on. It should be directly tied to the mission, and should be in the user's zone of proximal development.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: If possible, open the lesson file for the user by running a CLI command.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Each lesson should link via HTML anchors to other lessons and reference documents.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Each lesson should recommend a primary source for the user to read or watch. This should be the most high-quality, high-trust resource you found on the topic.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Each lesson should contain a reminder to ask followup questions to the agent. The agent is their teacher, and can assist with anything that's unclear.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Assets

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Lessons are built from reusable **components**, stored in `./assets/`: stylesheets, quiz widgets, simulators, diagram helpers — anything a second lesson could reuse.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Reuse is the default, not the exception. Before authoring a lesson, read `./assets/` and build from the components already there. When a lesson needs something new and reusable, write it as a component in `./assets/` and link to it — never inline code a future lesson would duplicate.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A shared stylesheet is the first component every workspace earns: every lesson links it, so the lessons look like one consistent course rather than a pile of one-offs. As the workspace grows, so should the component library.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## The Mission

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Every lesson should be tied into the mission - the reason that the user is interested in learning about the topic.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: If the user is unclear about the mission, or the `MISSION.md` is not populated, your first job should be to question the user on why they want to learn this.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Failing to understand the mission will mean knowledge acquisition is not grounded in real-world goals. Lessons will feel too abstract. You will have no way of judging what the user should do next.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Missions may change as the user develops more skills and knowledge. This is normal - make sure to update the `MISSION.md` and add a learning record to capture the change. Confirm with the user before changing the mission.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Zone Of Proximal Development

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Each lesson, the user should always feel as if they are being challenged 'just enough'.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The user may specify an exact thing they want to learn. If they don't, figure out their zone of proximal development by:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Reading their `learning-records`

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Figuring out the right thing to teach them based on their mission

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Teach the most relevant thing that fits in their zone of proximal development

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Knowledge

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Lessons should be designed around a skill the user is going to learn. The knowledge in the lesson should be only what's required to acquire that skill. You teach the knowledge first, then get the user to practice the skills via an interactive feedback loop.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Knowledge should first be gathered from trusted resources. Use `RESOURCES.md` to keep track of them. Lessons should be littered with citations - links to external resources to back up any claim made. This increases the trustworthiness of the lesson.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: For acquiring knowledge, difficulty is the enemy. It eats working memory you need for understanding.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Skills

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: If knowledge is all about acquisition, skills are about durability and flexibility. Make the knowledge stick.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: For skill acquisition, difficulty is the tool. Effortful retrieval is what builds storage strength. Skills should be taught through interactive lessons. There are several tools at your disposal:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Interactive lessons, using quizzes and light in-browser tasks

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Lessons which guide the user through a list of real-world steps to take (for instance, yoga poses)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Each of these should be based on a **feedback loop**, where the user receives feedback on their performance. This feedback loop should be as tight as possible, giving feedback immediately - and ideally automatically.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: For quizzes, each answer should be exactly the same number of words (and characters, if possible). Don't give the user any clues about the answer through formatting.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Acquiring Wisdom

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Wisdom comes from true real-world interaction - testing your skills outside the learning environment.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: When the user asks a question that appears to require wisdom, your default posture should be to attempt to answer - but to ultimately delegate to a **community**.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A community is a place (online or offline) where the user can test their skills in the real world. This might be a forum, a subreddit, a real-world class (budget permitting) or a local interest group.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: You should attempt to find high-reputation communities the user can join. If the user expresses a preference that they don't want to join a community, respect it.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Reference Documents

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: While creating lessons, you should also create reference documents. Lessons can reference these documents - they are useful for tracking raw units of knowledge useful across lessons.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Lessons will rarely be revisited later - reference documents will be. They should be the compressed essence of the lesson, in a format designed for quick reference.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Some learning topics lend themselves to reference:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Syntax and code snippets for programming

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Algorithms and flowcharts for processes

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Yoga poses and sequences for yoga

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Exercises and routines for fitness

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Glossaries for any topic with its own nomenclature

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Glossaries, in particular, are an essential reference. Once one is created, it should be adhered to in every lesson.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## `NOTES.md`

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The user will sometimes express preferences of how they want to be taught, or things you should keep in mind. This is the place to record those preferences, so you can refer back to them when designing lessons or working with the user.
